```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(spLeakage)
```

## Interpret each check in relation to the task

Spatial distance is one description of a prediction task. Shared groups,
covariate support, time ordering and overlapping predictor-extraction windows
can also matter. The functions below report those features. Their historical
names contain "leakage", but a flagged feature does not automatically establish
predictive bias or a violation of the intended task.

These extensions are outside the focused spatial methodological paper. They are
not a validated system for combining separate flags into a corrected accuracy.

```{r data}
set.seed(21)
d <- data.frame(x = runif(120), y = runif(120))
d$z <- sin(3 * d$x) + rnorm(120, sd = 0.3)
folds <- sample(rep_len(1:5, nrow(d)))
g <- as.matrix(expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10),
                          y = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10)))
target <- prediction_target(grid = g)
```

## Spatial mismatch

```{r spatial}
detect_leakage(d, folds, target, response = "z", coords = c("x", "y"))
```

Positive `SLI_rho` means greater average specified nearest-neighbour correlation
in validation. It does not establish the sign of error bias for every learner.
Inspect unsigned mismatch and distribution crossings as well.

## Shared groups and co-located observations

Copying the same response into training and test sets is a direct reuse problem.
Distinct measurements at a shared site are different: they may have independent
observation noise, and their suitability depends on whether the prediction task
concerns new sites or further measurements at observed sites.

```{r groups}
dd <- rbind(d, d[1:10, ])  # deliberately copy complete observations
split <- sample(rep_len(1:5, nrow(dd)))
detect_group_leakage(dd, split, coords = c("x", "y"))
grouped <- group_kfold(dd, k = 5, coords = c("x", "y"))
detect_group_leakage(dd, grouped, coords = c("x", "y"))$frac_leaked
```

`frac_leaked` is a historical field name for the fraction of test observations
sharing a group with training observations. Keeping groups together addresses a
new-group prediction task; it does not establish accurate validation for every
possible target.

## Covariate support

```{r features}
d$covariate <- d$x + d$y + rnorm(nrow(d), sd = 0.1)
newdata <- data.frame(covariate = seq(1, 3, length.out = 100))
detect_feature_leakage(d, folds, covariates = "covariate", newdata = newdata)
```

Differences between training, test and target covariates can reveal extrapolation
that geographic distances miss. Inspect the particular predictor and its response
relationship. A feature-distance score is not a general loss estimate.

## Overlapping extraction windows

```{r windows}
detect_extraction_leakage(d, folds, radius = 0.08, coords = c("x", "y"))
```

The output counts overlapping predictor windows. Shared pixels are not necessarily
inappropriate when those same predictors are available at deployment. Check
whether feature construction used unavailable outcomes or information, and whether
validation reproduces the intended prediction setting.

## Time ordering and joint space–time distance

```{r temporal}
st <- d[rep(1:20, each = 6), ]; st$time <- rep(1:6, 20)
st_folds <- sample(rep_len(1:5, nrow(st)))
detect_temporal_leakage(st, st_folds, time = "time")
forward <- temporal_kfold(st, k = 4, time = "time")
detect_temporal_leakage(st, forward, time = "time")$lookahead_frac
```

Training on future records can violate a prospective forecasting task. It need
not violate a retrospective reconstruction task. The nearest-record lookahead
fraction is a descriptive check, not a complete audit of all information used by
a forecasting pipeline.

```{r spacetime}
detect_st_leakage(st, st_folds, time = "time", coords = c("x", "y"))
```

The joint distance depends on how space and time are scaled. A larger joint
contrast does not establish a correspondingly larger predictive bias.

## Trend and combined reporting

```{r trend}
trend_strength(d, "z", coords = c("x", "y"))
audit_workflow(dd, split, target, response = "z", coords = c("x", "y"))
```

Trend strength describes the response variation explained by a fitted coordinate
surface. It does not measure extrapolation error. The combined report brings
these checks together without using an arbitrary letter grade to certify the
workflow. See `vignette("quantify-correct")` for the limits of score-comparison
and experimental accuracy-rescaling functions.
